meta.purpose: Palo Duro fixes: P7861 Residue Header to gathering, 150 miles, Washita County OK to Roberts County TX, data center tag removed; P7862 Palo Duro to operating; interstate service project staged as a new row in staged_new.json

verifications.note: The FERC order issuing certificates for docket CP25-531, dated March 19, 2026 (194 FERC 61,220). It describes the 150 mile, 16 and 20 inch Header Pipeline from Washita County, Oklahoma, to Roberts County, Texas, as part of the gathering system that Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering) owns and operates. It describes the 275 mile, 16 inch PD Pipeline from Nolan County to Wheeler County, Texas, as currently operating and gathering gas. It approves interstate service on the northern 61 miles of the PD Pipeline plus 80,000 dekatherms a day of leased Header capacity.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Status stays operating. The FERC order of March 19, 2026, says Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering) owns and operates the Header Pipeline today.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Changed from transmission to gathering. The FERC order calls the Header Pipeline part of the non-jurisdictional Anadarko Gathering System, which has more than 3,000 miles of pipe and about 2,750 connected wells. Only a leased slice of its capacity becomes interstate service, and that slice is the new row for the interstate project.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Changed from transmission to both transmission and gathering. The FERC order says the line currently gathers gas. Under the amended plan the northern 61 miles, in Childress, Collingsworth and Wheeler counties, become interstate transmission, and the southern part is to be sold to an affiliate and kept as gathering. The row stays whole rather than being split in two.
